newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares weaker on high interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares weaker on high interest rates.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index shed 81.12 points to 10,028.18 on Monday as investors continued sidelining the bourse in favour of the local money market, brokers said.
"We're losing points everyday because the outlook is for interest rates to continue rising and that's attracting money away from equities to the local money market," one broker said.

He added that a continued stable Zimbabwe dollar despite rising annual inflation, which edged up to 22.4 percent in April from 19.9 percent the previous month, rendered the local money less competitive against other currencies and this could be keeping foreign investors away.

The index was weighed down on Monday by losses in agricultural investors Chemco which shed 200 cents to 3,800, bankers Barclays, down 100 cents to 2,700 and National Tyre Services which put off 75 cents to 350.

Other counters to lose were cement maker Porthold, hotel and retail giants Meikles, timber producers Border and cable manufacturers Bicc Cafca, which all lost 50 cents to 1,600, 2,650, 1,550 and 350 respectively.
The seven share mining index added 1.27 points to close at 1,014.36, largely buoyed by a 100 cent gain to 1,200 in gold producer Falcon.
